name: My Thai Chicken Wraps
headnote: A one-line headnote from submitter gztg44: these lettuce wraps are her home version of a restaurant appetizer she loves, and her family asks for them weekly. The site's own blurb adds that rotisserie chicken is re-sauteed with garlic, ginger, basil, hoisin and soy for extra flavour, and that store-bought Thai peanut sauce finishes each wrap. No technique explanation is given beyond simmering until the liquid is absorbed.
comment_digest: The most helpful review (24 votes, Lori) says the dish is too sweet as written and recommends dropping the sugar or cutting the hoisin; this is by far the most repeated correction, with others halving the sugar and one reducing hoisin to 1/4 cup with good results. A few instead want more hoisin. The step people get wrong is the slaw timing: several report it turning to mush and advise stirring the coleslaw mix in at the very end. Common additions are water chestnuts, red pepper flakes, scallions, extra basil and crisp fried rice noodles. Substitutions that work include ground chicken, poached breast, chicken thighs, broccoli slaw, rice vinegar or lime juice for the white vinegar, and honey for hoisin. Butter or Bibb lettuce is preferred; tortillas and rice bowls also get good reports. Other complaints: soupy, messy, high in sodium.
